The viscosity measurement reveals that these phosphoric acids are fragile glass-formers with fragility in the range of 95 − 150. The  T g  values determined from both conductivity and viscosity measurements are consistent with the result of previous DSC measurements. We have also con fi rmed that NMR line width analysis indeed overestimates the glass-transition temperature and therefore is not a suitable method for  T g  determination. Finally, our Walden plot analysis indicates that phosphoric acids behave like other aqueous acidic solutions at high temperatures but exhibit moderate decoupling between ionic conductivity and structural dynamics in the vicinity of the glass transition. ■ AUTHOR INFORMATION

mechanism_relevant_findings: Phosphoric acids behave like other aqueous acidic solutions at high temperatures but exhibit moderate decoupling between ionic conductivity and structural dynamics in the vicinity of the glass transition.
There are two principal mechanisms recognized for proton transport in liquids: the vehicle mechanism and the Grotthuss mechanism.
Proton migration in phosphoric acid is thought to be achieved through the Grotthuss mechanism, characterized by local proton hopping within hydrogen bonds.

limitations: Previous studies on electrical conductivity of phosphoric acids are limited to high temperatures.
The appropriate method for determining the glass-transition temperature is still a subject of controversy.
